PB- and 3-Mc-type PCB isomers and PCB congeners, respectively, are capable of modulating hepatocellular necrotic responses to both bromobenzene- and acetaminophene-induced cytotoxicity.

the PB-type isomers and congenres are more likely to increase hepatotoxicity of both acetaminophen and bromobenzene whereas the 3-MC type isomers and congenrs are more likely to potentiate only the toxicity of acetaminophene.

PB-type PCBs, which are the predominant PCBs in the environment, can increase susceptibility to bromobenzenes, whereas 3-MC-like PCBs, which have been found to be the most prevalent PCBs in human tissues, increase susceptibility to acetaminophen.
